reuse.why: Reuses setBudget, getSheetValue, batchMessages, isTrackingBudget and the shared extractTagsFromText for the #fixed tag; the new action computes its amount from the existing sum-amount sheet cell rather than a new query.

duplication.why: The three copied category queries and setZero's query are collapsed into one getMonthWideCategories; only the pre-existing per-action income/tracking guard is repeated once more in setLastMonthSpending.

placement.why: The selection rule lives in budget/actions.ts beside the actions that use it and the new method is registered in budget/app.ts like its siblings.

scope.why: Edits are limited to the month-wide actions, the new handler, its registration, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: One function now decides which categories month-wide actions touch (hidden, template, #fixed, with an explicit flag), so future rules land in one place; the income guard still lives in each action and the rule is split between SQL and a JS tag filter.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All six month-wide actions take their category set from getMonthWideCategories; copyPreviousMonth intersects its budget rows with it.

disguised_duplication.where: The only repeated logic is the literal 'is_income === 1 && !isTrackingBudget()' guard in setLastMonthSpending, copied openly from the existing actions.

abstraction_drift.where: getMonthWideCategories gained only the includeHiddenCategories parameter (step 4) that selects the hidden filter; the #fixed rule (step 3) was added as a uniform filter and the new action (step 2) calls it like the others.
